task.title: Publish the desktop app from this repository's releases
task.description:
Cut desktop builds from this repository, and retire the one they come from today.

Depends on CI: a release path that publishes what nothing verified is worse than no release path. Depends on pre-release support: the first desktop release rides the CLI's `v0.6.0-rc1`.

## Two numbers, with a cascade

Decided 2026-09-15; amended 2026-09-19 with Dylan.

- **The CLI keeps `vX.Y.Z`** and everything about its release path is unchanged.
- **The app has its own sequence**, tagged `desktop-vX.Y.Z`, with the same grammar as the CLI's including `-rcN` pre-releases. A desktop release can be cut on its own whenever the app needs one; a desktop-only fix never bumps the CLI.
- **The sequence starts at the CLI's number.** The first desktop release is `desktop-v0.6.0-rc1`, the companion of `v0.6.0-rc1`, so the two numbers read the same until a desktop-only release is ever cut.
- **Every CLI release cascades.** When `vX.Y.Z` (or `vX.Y.Z-rcN`) has published, `release.yml` cuts the companion desktop release automatically. The companion's version is the CLI's exact version when that orders after the newest `desktop-v*` tag; when it does not (a desktop-only release has moved ahead), the cascade fails loudly and says the desktop release has to be cut by hand with a chosen version. Nothing guesses a bump kind.
- **A pre-release cascades into a pre-release**: `v0.6.0-rc1` → `desktop-v0.6.0-rc1`, flagged as a pre-release on GitHub, and it refreshes the rolling `desktop-latest` release like any other desktop release (decided with Dylan: the site link and the app's update check follow the newest desktop release, pre-release or not, while the Homebrew tap never sees a pre-release).
- **The About panel shows both numbers**: the app's version and the version of the CLI it bundles. (The version line already shows the CLI's; the app's own comes from `package.json`, which the workflow stamps.)

## Which CLI a desktop build bundles

Never the working tree. The workflow builds the CLI at the newest `v*` tag reachable from the commit being released (`git describe --tags --match 'v*' --abbrev=0`), passed to `desktop/scripts/build-workbook.sh` as `WORKBOOK_REF`. For a companion release that is the CLI just published, tagged on the same commit, so `git describe` at that commit prints exactly the tag and the bundled binary reports it. For a desktop-only release it is the last CLI release, so unreleased Go changes on `main` never ride along inside the app. `npm start` still builds the working tree.

**One binary per target.** The stage script builds for the host by default; the workflow stages once per platform and architecture it packages (`GOOS`/`GOARCH` passed through to `go build`, output under `desktop/build/<goos>-<goarch>/`), and `desktop/scripts/after-pack.js` copies the binary matching the bundle being packed into its resources, falling back to `desktop/build/workbook` for a local `npm run dist`. The `extraResources` entries in `package.json` that copied one host binary into every bundle go away; the resource path the app reads (`workbook` or `workbook.exe` beside the license in `Resources/`) is unchanged.

## Where releases live

Each `desktop-vX.Y.Z` gets a permanent GitHub Release in this repository: macOS (arm64, x64; DMG and ZIP), Linux (x64, arm64; AppImage and deb), Windows (x64, arm64; NSIS), plus electron-builder's feed files (`latest-mac.yml`, `latest-linux.yml`, `latest.yml`). The same workflow then refreshes a rolling release tagged `desktop-latest` with the same assets, replacing what was there (`gh release upload --clobber`, moving the tag). Installer names carry no version (`Workbench-arm64.dmg`), so the rolling release's download URLs are stable and the site can link them.

Uploads go through `gh release`, the way `scripts/publish-release.sh` already works, not through electron-builder's publisher: the app's `build.publish` is the generic provider and only says where the app reads its feed. The versioned release is create-once, and a rerun with different assets is refused, as for the CLI.

## The update check

electron-updater's GitHub provider walks the repository's release feed and skips any tag that is not plain semver, so it cannot share a release list with the CLI: `desktop-v1.4.0` is invisible to it and `v0.6.0` carries no feed file. The app therefore uses the generic provider pointed at `https://github.com/dgoings/workbook/releases/download/desktop-latest`. The move already writes that into `package.json`.

The macOS behavior comes across unchanged. Those builds carry an ad-hoc signature rather than a Developer ID one, and Squirrel.Mac silently refuses to install over a bundle it cannot verify, so `quitAndInstall` returns having done nothing while the user believes they upgraded. The Mac path downloads the DMG and opens it in Finder instead. Windows uses electron-updater's native download-and-restart flow.

## Cutting a desktop release

`desktop-release.yml` is reachable three ways, like `release.yml`: a pushed `desktop-v*` tag, a `workflow_call` from the cascade in `release.yml` (which tags the same commit and calls it directly, because a tag pushed with the default token starts no workflow), and a `workflow_dispatch` taking an existing tag for a rerun. There is no separate cut-desktop-release button for now (decided with Dylan: no extra machinery); a desktop-only release is cut by hand by pushing a `desktop-vX.Y.Z` tag on `main`, and CONTRIBUTING says so. `release.yml`'s `v*` trigger does not match `desktop-v*`, and the desktop workflow's trigger must not match `v*`.

The workflow validates the tag with the CLI's version grammar (a `scripts/validate-desktop-release-tag.sh` that strips `desktop-v` and reuses `release-version.sh`), writes the version into `desktop/package.json` before packaging (`npm version --no-git-tag-version`), so the checked-in `0.0.0` is never released, and runs the shell's own checks before building.

The cascade job in `release.yml` runs after the CLI's publish job succeeds and is not gated by the `release` environment a second time: the one approval covers the run. It computes the desktop tag with `scripts/plan-desktop-release.sh --cli-version X`, which prints `desktop-vX` or fails per the rule above, tags, pushes, and calls the desktop workflow.

`scripts/publish-release.sh` is untouched: desktop assets live in desktop releases, so its exact-asset-count check on rerun still holds.

## Signing

Ad-hoc signed and unnotarized on macOS, in `desktop/scripts/after-pack.js`, exactly as Workbench ships today; first launch needs right-click Open. Windows installers are unsigned for now: the Azure Trusted Signing plumbing waits until there is a certificate to plumb (decided with Dylan: nothing speculative in the first cut). Notarization is its own task.

## Verification

The workflow tests in `scripts/release_workflow_test.go` grow to cover `desktop-release.yml` (reachable by tag push, call and dispatch; checks out the tag it publishes; concurrency keyed on the tag; pinned actions and runners; scripts it calls exist) and the cascade (the job exists, needs the publish job, calls the desktop workflow with the tag). `plan-desktop-release.sh`, `validate-desktop-release-tag.sh` and the desktop publisher get script tests with fixture repositories and the fake `gh`, like their CLI counterparts. The per-target staging gets a test beside `desktop_stage_test.go`. The first real run is the `v0.6.0-rc1` cut, which Dylan triggers.

## Last step

Archive `tylerkilgore/workbench` once a `desktop-v*` has been cut from here and verified to install. The one existing install is not migrated.

comments.author: a@example.com
comments.body: Local finding 2026-09-15: on macOS 26.6.2 (Darwin 25), electron-builder 26's DMG step fails in the bundled dmgbuild (plistlib.InvalidFileException while parsing hdiutil output; dmg-builder@1.2.5). The .app and ZIP targets build and the ad-hoc signature verifies. CI's macOS runner may not hit this; if it does, the DMG target needs a newer dmg-builder or a different hdiutil invocation before the macOS update flow (which downloads the DMG) can work.

comments.author: a@example.com
comments.body: Follow-up on the DMG failure: it is hdiutil convert on macOS 26.6.2 deadlocking with itself, not a third-party agent. The -debug trace shows the output file created with a mandatory exclusive lock (OpenLockFriendly flags 0xE02 -> 0xE26), then reopened with a second exclusive lock for the header update, which fails with errno 35 (EAGAIN). It fails for UDZO, ULFO and UDRO from any source or destination; a fresh file locks fine from another process; hdiutil create -srcfolder works; and -c.dmg.format=UDRW builds a mountable 315 MB DMG. Locally, UDRW is the workaround. CI runners on macOS 14/15 should be unaffected; if the publish workflow ever runs on macOS 26 it needs either UDRW or a dmgbuild that avoids the second locked open.

comments.author: a@example.com
comments.body: PR 140 on GitHub (dgoings/workbook): desktop-release.yml on macos-15/ubuntu-24.04/windows-2025 with pinned actions, cascade jobs in release.yml, validate/plan/publish scripts with tests, per-target CLI staging and afterPack placement, detectUpdateChannel false and no NSIS universal installer. Adversarial review rehearsed the publisher under dash with electron-builder real asset names and caught two first-run breakers (rc channel manifests; desktop-tag stamping), both fixed. Not run end to end; the v0.6.0-rc1 cut is the proof.
